transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Park (Redwood SE), Eli Summers (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Atlas Data Eng), Ravi Patel (Atlas ML Eng), Samir Khan (Atlas Security), Priya Mehta (Atlas Product), Diego Ruiz (Atlas Infra)

Summary (auto): Quick check-in, focus on clearing VPC service account blockers and scheduling benchmark run.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see the atlas team again. quick roll call?
[00:08] Lena: lena here, hi.
[00:10] Ravi: ravi, ml.
[00:12] Samir: samir - security.
[00:13] Priya: priya product.
[00:15] Diego: diego infra.
[00:18] Jordan: jordan from redwood, hello.
[00:20] Maya: great, quick agenda, 1) onboarding blockers 2) env readiness for benchmarks 3) security docs and next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Priya: yes that's perfect.
[00:30] Lena: quick status - we created the project and started to provision the shared bucket. we ran into permission errors when trying to attach the service account to the compute nodes, it looks like our infra team needs to allow the cross-project iam binding.
[00:46] Diego: yeah i tried the role binding but our org policy blocked the custom role, i'm following up with the cloud team.
[00:52] Jordan: ok that's the main gating item for running the benchmark. We can also run a hosted baseline on redwood's side with a sanitized sample if you prefer, that would give fast numbers but not full network characteristics.
[01:04] Ravi: we want to see both if possible - hosted for quick perf numbers and private to validate latency in our network.
[01:10] Maya: makes sense. Jordan, can you propose the baseline tests? like sequence length, concurrency, target qps?
[01:18] Jordan: yes - plan to run two sets: 1) baseline hosted run using 10k short-sequence requests (avg 32 tokens) for throughput/latency and token cost; 2) private deployment run with a smaller 2k sample but hitting full 1k token sequences to exercise kv cache behavior and memory. concurrency sweep 8/32/128 depending on VM/pool.
[01:40] Samir: from security side, we need to see SOC2, network diagram, encryption at rest keys, and key management options - do you support customer-managed keys?
[01:50] Maya: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. we'll send the security pack with SOC2 + network diagram. for hosted we provide encryption but not customer-managed keys unless on Dedicated/Private.
[02:04] Samir: noted. also, logging and audit retention - how long are logs kept and can we forward them to our splunk?
[02:12] Eli: we can configure audit log forwarding, retention varies by tier, we'll include per-route log retention options in the doc.
[02:20] Ravi: on the model side, did you recommend any quantization or model family for our NLU tasks? we saw some throughput numbers for redwood-7b-quant.
[02:29] Jordan: for latency sensitive, start with base 7B quantized profile - it gives good lat/throughput. we can suggest 4-bit quantization profile for private dedicated if memory is tight; we'll share recommended kernel/profile mapping.
[02:45] Priya: what's the expected cost delta between hosted baseline vs Dedicated for our volume (est 10M tokens / month)?
[02:53] Maya: rough back-of-envelope: hosted at list is higher per-token but zero infra ops; Dedicated with reserved capacity tends to be 30-50% lower per-token at scale depending on utilization. we'll send a tailored cost projection once we see real qps and sequences.
[03:10] Lena: on dataset - we will upload a sanitized sample this week but need help with the exact format. what's required?
[03:18] Jordan: csv or jsonl with prompt/response fields, include tokenization notes if you pre-tokenize. schema: id, prompt, expected_response, metadata (optional). we'll put a quick template in the shared drive.
[03:29] Lena: ok we'll match that.
[03:31] Diego: network - for private deployment we need VPC peering details, GW rules, and whether we need a NAT for outbound. also do you require direct connect or is peering enough?
[03:42] Maya: peering is usually sufficient but depends on latency needs. for strict isolation some customers prefer Direct Connect/MPLS; we'll document options and provide a checklist.
[03:52] Samir: any special ports or subnets?
[03:55] Jordan: mostly HTTPS outbound, a handful of control ports for health checks, and SSH only if you choose on-prem debug access; we'll include exact port list.
[04:05] Priya: can we run a quick smoke test next week? just to validate pipeline before the full benchmark.
[04:09] Maya: yes, that would help. Jordan can run the hosted smoke run as soon as sample is uploaded, then coordinate private smoke after service account is fixed.
[04:18] Jordan: i'll prepare harness and a short smoke test script. i'll also include a small benchmark spreadsheet template to report latency/percentiles and token cost.
[04:28] Ravi: how will you measure tail latency and p95/p99?
[04:31] Jordan: we'll capture per-request latencies, compute p50/p95/p99, and show server-side vs client-observed latency; for private runs we'll highlight KV cache hit rates as well.
[04:40] Samir: one more - are there data retention controls for inputs/outputs? we need to ensure no logs persist beyond retention windows for PCI considerations.
[04:49] Eli: yes there are per-customer retention policies; for Private/Dedicated you can set retention or disable logging. we'll include options in the security pack.
[04:58] Lena: timeline check: we want initial benchmark by 2025-08-12, assuming we can get the sample uploaded by 2025-08-08 and infra fixes by 2025-08-09.
[05:10] Maya: that's reasonable. i'll send the security docs by 2025-08-07 and jordan will run baseline once dataset received.
[05:18] Priya: can you also include model regression checks? we need to ensure no drop in NLU intent accuracy after quantization.
[05:25] Jordan: yes we'll add a small eval harness to compute intent accuracy and include that alongside perf metrics.
[05:32] Diego: on the IAM side, what minimal permissions does the service account need?
[05:36] Jordan: read/write to the shared bucket, ability to attach to compute instance (or access to the endpoint for hosted), and network egress to Redwood endpoints. we'll convert to a minimal role and share a terraform snippet.
[05:48] Samir: ok sounds good. please include any audit commands we can run to validate.
[05:52] Eli: we'll include a checklist for validation steps.
[05:56] Maya: quick recap then next steps - recap: 1) Atlas uploads sanitized dataset by 2025-08-08 (Lena) 2) Infra fixes IAM binding by 2025-08-09 (Diego) 3) Redwood shares security pack + pricing by 2025-08-07 (Maya) 4) Redwood runs hosted baseline and smoke when dataset available (Jordan) 5) schedule VPC deep dive week of 2025-08-11 (all). any additions?
[06:22] Priya: no that's all.
[06:24] Lena: sounds good.
[06:26] Maya: great thanks everyone, i'll follow up in email with links to the drive and action items.
[06:31] Jordan: thanks all.
[06:33] End

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and auto-caption artifacts. References to product names: "redwood-7b-quant", "Dedicated", "Private", "KV cache". Shared artifacts referenced: security pack (link to be emailed), benchmark spreadsheet template (to be uploaded to shared drive).
